name: Walk-Behind Floor Scrubber
definition: A powered commercial scrubber-dryer that applies solution, mechanically agitates a hard floor and recovers dirty liquid while an operator walks behind and guides the machine.
includedScope: Traction-drive and manually propelled walk-behind machines
Disc, cylindrical/roller and orbital walk-behind configurations
excludedScope: Single-disc floor machines without liquid recovery
Domestic floor washers and carpet extractors
headline: Walk-behind floor scrubber types, route fit, performance and buyer checks
description: Technical reference for walk-behind scrubber dryers covering operator format, deck and recovery systems, representative models, comparable metrics and site verification.
metaDescription: Walk-behind floor scrubber guide covering types, working widths, tanks, batteries, representative models and procurement checks.
disclaimer: Independent category reference, not model-specific purchasing, safety, chemical or floor-compatibility advice. Verify the exact regional product, manual, route, floor, battery, charger and service support.

heroImageCaption: Official TASKI application image showing a walk-behind scrubber in a healthcare corridor. It does not establish universal floor, noise or infection-control suitability.

keyFacts.label: Category boundary
keyFacts.value: Operator walks behind and directly guides the machine; manufacturer classification takes priority over width or area claims.
keyFacts.evidence: Reviewed official product pages use the stated operating format and equipment architecture for the named machines.
keyFacts.scope: Named models and reviewed regional configurations; no universal dimensional threshold is inferred.

keyFacts.label: Primary work interface
keyFacts.value: A powered scrub deck followed by squeegee and vacuum recovery.
keyFacts.evidence: Official product pages document disc, cylindrical/roller or orbital heads with solution and recovery systems.
keyFacts.scope: Exact brush, pad, nozzle, floor and consumable configuration.

keyFacts.label: Productivity boundary
keyFacts.value: Manufacturer area rates are source-specific, not achieved-site guarantees
keyFacts.evidence: Official sources publish model-specific widths, speeds or stated productivity figures under their own reporting conventions.
keyFacts.scope: Named manufacturer figures only; no cross-brand normalization or ranking.

keyFacts.label: Configuration boundary
keyFacts.value: Traction, deck, battery, charger and dosing options can change within one model family.
keyFacts.evidence: Reviewed product families publish multiple head and energy configurations.
keyFacts.scope: Delivered product number, voltage, battery or cable, consumables and local service terms.

systemFlow.name: Solution delivery
systemFlow.componentFamily: Fresh-water tank, dosing path and control
systemFlow.role: Meters approved cleaning solution to the working area.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturer manuals and pages document solution tanks and delivery controls.
systemFlow.scope: Exact model, chemistry and flow setting.

systemFlow.name: Mechanical agitation
systemFlow.role: Loosens soil through the selected brush or pad interface.
systemFlow.evidence: Official pages document model-specific deck choices.
systemFlow.scope: Deck, consumable, floor and pressure are configuration-specific.

systemFlow.name: Squeegee collection
systemFlow.role: Channels liquid toward the suction path.
systemFlow.evidence: Commercial scrubber documentation identifies squeegee recovery assemblies.
systemFlow.scope: Exact blade material, geometry and adjustment.

systemFlow.name: Vacuum recovery
systemFlow.componentFamily: Vacuum motor, hose and recovery tank
systemFlow.role: Collects dirty solution for controlled disposal.
systemFlow.evidence: Official specifications publish separate recovery systems and tanks.
systemFlow.scope: Achieved dryness depends on setup, floor, blades and speed.

variants.name: Compact manually propelled
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator supplies guidance and some travel force
variants.limitations: Smaller tanks can increase support time.
variants.evidence: Hako positions B25 as a compact walk-behind.
variants.scope: Named model; no fixed size threshold.

variants.name: Traction-drive medium walk-behind
variants.operatorRelationship: Powered travel reduces push effort but still requires walking
variants.spaceConstraints: Door, squeegee and turning envelope remain critical
variants.limitations: Travel assist does not establish ergonomic suitability.
variants.evidence: Tennant, Nilfisk, Kärcher and Hako publish powered walk-behind models.

variants.name: Disc, roller or orbital deck
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator selects approved settings and consumables
variants.spaceConstraints: Deck and squeegee width change fit
variants.limitations: Deck labels do not prove equivalent results.
variants.evidence: Tennant and Kärcher publish multiple deck architectures.

performanceMetrics.name: Working width
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Exact head configuration and source unit
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Width alone does not establish route fit or achieved output.

performanceMetrics.name: Solution and recovery capacity
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Nominal tank values, not usable-cycle proof
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Tank size does not include travel, refill or cleaning time.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official specifications publish separate tank capacities.

performanceMetrics.name: Theoretical area performance
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: A planning input based on stated width and travel assumptions
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not treat theoretical output as achieved site productivity.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official pages publish model-specific theoretical figures for selected machines.
performanceMetrics.scope: Source figures only; no cross-brand normalization.

performanceMetrics.name: Battery runtime and charging
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Supports shift, charger and battery planning
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Exact battery chemistry, capacity, charger and duty
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Maximum runtime is not guaranteed shift output.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Manufacturers publish battery or charger options by configuration.

applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Route geometry and support time should be measured before selecting width or tank size.
applicationFit.basis: Documented working widths and tank systems.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Map doors, turns, refill points and disposal route; run a witnessed trial.
applicationFit.engineeringCheck: Record achieved clean-and-dry area per labor hour.
applicationFit.evidence: Manufacturers position reviewed scrubbers for commercial hard-floor cleaning.
applicationFit.assessment: Route geometry and support time should be measured before selecting width or tank size.

applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Daytime suitability requires local sound, traffic and residual-moisture acceptance.
applicationFit.basis: Official application positioning and model-specific sound data.
applicationFit.limitations: A marketing application image is not a universal safety result.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Trial during the intended operating window and document controls.
applicationFit.engineeringCheck: Check sound method, visibility, stopping distance and dryness.
applicationFit.evidence: Official sources show or position selected machines in public and healthcare settings.
applicationFit.scope: Exact site procedure and regional model.
applicationFit.assessment: Daytime suitability requires local sound, traffic and residual-moisture acceptance.

applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Deck and squeegee choice should be proven on the actual surface.
applicationFit.basis: Manufacturers offer disc, roller and orbital heads plus different squeegees.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Use a soil-and-floor test panel in the acceptance trial.
applicationFit.engineeringCheck: Inspect edge cleaning, solution recovery and surface change.
applicationFit.evidence: Official pages document alternative deck systems and recovery features.
applicationFit.scope: Exact floor, soil, chemical and consumable.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Route fit, achieved productivity and recovery quality
procurementDecisions.assessment: Use a timed site trial including support work.
procurementDecisions.basis: Manufacturer figures omit some site variables.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Measure fill, travel, cleaning, dump and post-clean time.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Record floor area, obstacles, turns and achieved dryness.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources publish widths, tanks and selected theoretical output.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Battery chemistry, runtime, charger and opportunity-charging rules
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Assuming amp-hours or maximum runtime are directly comparable
procurementDecisions.assessment: Approve a complete energy package, not the machine alone.
procurementDecisions.basis: Battery options vary by product and market.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Require exact battery and charger part numbers in the quote.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Model energy, charging window, ventilation and electrical input.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources list model-specific battery choices.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Deck, consumable, chemistry and squeegee for every surface
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Treating one brush or pad as universal
procurementDecisions.assessment: Use a configuration matrix by floor and soil.
procurementDecisions.basis: Official ranges offer different working heads.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Compatibility must be confirmed by the machine and floor suppliers.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Require written approvals and sample cleaning.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Lock consumable part numbers and settings into the SOP.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Manufacturers publish disc, roller and orbital options on selected models.

engineeringChecks.reason: Nominal cleaning width is smaller than the machine or squeegee envelope.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Measure the complete route and demonstrate turns.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official pages publish dimensions and widths separately.

engineeringChecks.reason: Brush, pad, pressure and detergent can affect finish and recovery.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Obtain written approvals and trial the actual surface.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturers specify model-specific decks and chemical systems.
engineeringChecks.scope: Actual floor, coating, soil and chemistry.

engineeringChecks.reason: Decks, blades, batteries and chargers differ within a model family.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Record serial range and all consumable part numbers.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official product families expose multiple configurations.

standards.name: IEC 60335-2-72:2021
standards.applicability: Safety scope for powered ride-on and powered walk-behind commercial floor-treatment machines; it does not rank cleaning performance.
standards.evidence: IEC publishes the edition, date and scope.
standards.scope: Confirm regional adoption and the exact machine classification.

developments.title: IEC commercial floor-treatment safety edition published
developments.evidence: IEC catalogue records the publication date and scope.
